title: Finally building Level 1 of my steampunk action-platformer, "Hilted" (Made in Godot!) Video in comments
author: SpydrMonky24
selftext:
Hey everyone!  
I’m currently building **Hilted**, a 2D pixel-art steampunk action-platformer made in Godot. After spending a lot of time following tutorials, "vibe coding" with AI, and wrestling with placeholder blocks, I finally have the core mechanics locked down and I'm actively building out Level 1!

**The Core Concept:**  
You find an ancient hilt that lets you hot-swap different blades on the fly.  
**Blades = Progression:** You unlock new blades by defeating bosses or completing side quests.  
**Combat meets Traversal:** Each blade completely rewires your stats, playstyle, and movement mechanics. One blade might give you a grappling hook, another a dash, a double-jump, or temporary invisibility.  
**The Story & Theme:**  
It’s a steampunk world obsessed with transcending humanity, where technology and blind ambition push people way past their natural limits. The game is ultimately about the struggle to remain human in a world that views flesh as an obstacle.  
Right now, everything you see is placeholder art while I focus entirely on the game feel and level layout, but the process has been an absolute blast.  
I’d love to hear your thoughts on the mechanic!

Does a "hilt-swapping" system for traversal sound like something you'd want to play?

What kind of unique blade mechanic/movement combo would you want to see?
